title: /tools/source-health lists 4 of the 21 registered ranking sources and renders IDPTradeCalc as 0 rows because the count lookup is case-mismatched
claimUnderTest: The page subtitle reads 'Scraper status for every ranking source in the pipeline.' and the component docstring promises a per-source dot + record count + age.
observed: The strip is built from `source_health.source_runtime.enabled_sources`, which the scraper populates with exactly four scraper-side names ['IDPTradeCalc','KTC','KTC_TradeDB','KTC_WaiverDB']. The 17 CSV-loaded registry sources never appear. Worse, the per-row count lookup is `counts[src] || counts[src.toLowerCase()]`: source_counts is keyed 'ktc'/'idpTradeCalc', so 'KTC'->'ktc' resolves to 500 but 'IDPTradeCalc'->'idptradecalc' misses and renders 0 (shown as an em-dash). The per-source freshness map `health.sources` (22 real entries, correct camelCase keys) is fetched in the same payload and read with the same wrong keys, so `meta` is always {} and no per-source age is ever rendered.

reproduction.command:
# with the audit cookie and the :3001 edge proxy up
node -e "..." # see artifact; equivalently: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status | python -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin)['source_health'];print(d['source_runtime']['enabled_sources']);print(d['source_counts']);print(len(d['sources']))"
reproduction.expected: 21 source rows with counts and ages
reproduction.actual: Rendered DOM: 'Sources · 4' then 'IDPTradeCalc —', 'KTC 500 rows', 'KTC_TradeDB —', 'KTC_WaiverDB —'. No ages. enabled_sources=['IDPTradeCalc','KTC','KTC_TradeDB','KTC_WaiverDB']; source_counts={'ktc':500,'idpTradeCalc':900}; health.sources has 22 entries none of which are rendered.

numericProof.formula: rendered_rows = len(source_runtime.enabled_sources); rendered_count(src) = source_counts[src] or source_counts[lower(src)] or 0

userImpact: The one page an operator opens to answer 'is any source dead?' cannot answer it. A source that has been broken for weeks (the exact idpShow-cookie failure mode config/source_staleness.json was written for) shows nothing at all, and the retail IDP backbone that is in fact carrying 900 rows is displayed as having none — which reads as a total outage of the source the whole IDP board rests on.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A25-F14 covers critical-source flagging in the contract validator, not this page. No prior finding names /tools/source-health.

whatWorks: The underlying data IS in the payload: /api/status.source_health.sources carries correct per-source lastFetched+ageHours for all 22 CSV sources, and served_source_coverage carries real per-source board counts for all 21 registry sources. Only the renderer's key set is wrong.
rootCause: The strip iterates the scraper's run-summary source names (a 4-item scraper-internal vocabulary) instead of the registry keys, and joins two maps that use different casing conventions without normalizing.
requiredRepair: Drive the strip from `served_source_coverage` + `health.sources` (both registry-keyed, both already in the payload); keep `enabled_sources`/`source_failures` only as an overlay for scraper-stage failures. Normalize keys through one helper.
dependencies: W05-F002 (the /api/status fields the page currently trusts are themselves 2-of-21).

title: /api/status source_health describes 2 of 21 sources: total_sources=2, source_counts covers ktc+idpTradeCalc only, and missing_sources is structurally always empty
claimUnderTest: `source_health.{total_sources, sources_with_data, source_counts, missing_sources}` reports scraper/source health.
observed: `_build_source_health_snapshot` derives all four fields from `payload['sites']`, which the scraper writes only for the two sources it scrapes itself. The live raw payload's `sites` is literally `[{key:'ktc',playerCount:500},{key:'idpTradeCalc',playerCount:900}]`. The 19 sources loaded from CSV at contract-build time are never in `sites`, so total_sources=2, sources_with_data=2, and `missing_sources` — the field whose name promises to name a dead source — can only ever list ktc or idpTradeCalc and is [] in every healthy and almost every unhealthy state. Compounding it, the same file carries three mutually inconsistent counts for KTC: sites.playerCount=500, siteStats.ktc.count=704, and rows actually carrying a ktc value=590.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['source_health']['total_sources'], d['source_health']['source_counts'], d['source_health']['missing_sources']); print(len(d['served_source_coverage']))"; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json'));print(d['sites']);print(d['siteStats'])"
reproduction.expected: total_sources=21, missing_sources able to name any dead registered source
reproduction.actual: total_sources=2, source_counts={'ktc':500,'idpTradeCalc':900}, missing_sources=[]; served_source_coverage in the same response has all 21

numericProof.formula: total_sources = len({row['key'] for row in payload['sites']})

userImpact: Every consumer of source_health — the source-health page, the settings diagnostics, and any operator reading /api/status — is told the pipeline has two sources and that none are missing, in a system whose board is built from 21. A dead source is undetectable through this field.

priorFinding.note: F14 makes the narrower claim that only KTC/IDPTradeCalc can be flagged as a failed CRITICAL source. That is the same root cause (the scraper-side `sites`/run-summary vocabulary is 2-4 names wide) but F14 does not cover total_sources/source_counts/missing_sources or the three-way KTC count disagreement.

whatWorks: `served_source_coverage` in the SAME response is correct and complete (21 sources, real per-source board counts), and is what the deploy gate reads.
rootCause: source_health is derived from the scraper's own output shape, which predates the CSV-enrichment era; the 19 CSV sources join the board after the scraper is done and never write a `sites` row.
requiredRepair: Build source_health from the registry (`_RANKING_SOURCES` + `_per_source_freshness()` + `served_source_coverage`) and keep the scraper's `sites`/run-summary as an additional stage-level block. Delete or recompute `siteStats` (read by nothing outside the stripped view).

title: A source that fails by returning zero rows or by a vendor header rename is dropped from the board with an EMPTY sourceParseErrors — the schema probe covers 4 of 22 sources
claimUnderTest: `_enrich_from_source_csvs` collects `parse_errors`, which `validate_api_data_contract` turns into `source_parse_error:*` warnings and marks the contract degraded — i.e. an ingestion failure is surfaced.
observed: Only the file-missing branch appends a parse error. The two failure modes a real fetcher actually produces both return silently: (a) a header-only CSV (fetcher ran, scraped nothing) hits `if not csv_lookup: continue` with no error; (b) a vendor column rename produces a schema_mismatch ONLY for the four sources hard-coded in the probe at line 3584 (dlfSf, dlfIdp, fantasyProsIdp, fantasyProsSf) — the other 18, including the retail anchor ktcSfTep and the IDP backbone idpTradeCalc, fall through the alias lookup and vanish with parse_errors == [].

reproduction.command:
.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import sys,json,shutil,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'.')
from src.api.data_contract import _enrich_from_source_csvs
full=json.load(open('/tmp/w05_full.json'))
rows=[{'canonicalName':r.get('canonicalName'),'displayName':r.get('displayName'),'position':r.get('position')} for r in full['playersArray']]
def run(mut):
    tmp=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); (tmp/'CSVs').mkdir()
    shutil.copytree('CSVs/site_raw', tmp/'CSVs'/'site_raw'); mut(tmp)
    errs=[]; idx=_enrich_from_source_csvs([dict(r) for r in rows], parse_errors=errs, csv_root=tmp)
    return {k:len(v) for k,v in idx.items()}, errs
def rename(key):
    def m(tmp):
        p=tmp/'CSVs'/'site_raw'/f'{key}.csv'; L=p.read_text().splitlines(); L[0]='colA,colB'; p.write_text('\n'.join(L))
    return m
for k in ['dlfSf','otcffbSf','ktcSfTep','fantasyCalc']:
    c,e=run(rename(k)); print(k, c.get(k), e)
EOF
reproduction.expected: every source that vanishes appends a parse error
reproduction.actual: dlfSf None [{'error':'schema_mismatch',...}]; otcffbSf None []; ktcSfTep None []; fantasyCalc None []. Header-only CSV for otcffbSf: entries None, parse_errors []. Deleted file: parse_errors [{'error':'file_not_found'}].

userImpact: When a vendor renames a column — the single most common real-world source break — that source's votes silently leave the blend and every affected player's consensus value shifts, with no warning on any surface. The CI watchdog (watchdog_contract_coverage.py) does catch it on the next 2h cycle, but the served board is wrong for up to that window and the running server never says so.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the schema-probe coverage gap or the header-only silent path. Distinct from PRIOR-A25-F00, which is about freshness stamps.

whatWorks: The file-missing path is honest: it appends {'error':'file_not_found'}, logs a warning, and flips the contract to degraded. The four probed sources behave correctly.
rootCause: The schema probe was added reactively for the two vendors that had actually broken, and was never generalized. The generic reader treats 'no recognised columns' as 'no rows' rather than 'wrong schema'.
requiredRepair: Make the probe universal: for every source, assert at least one name-alias column AND one value-or-rank-alias column in the header; emit schema_mismatch otherwise. Separately, emit `source_empty:{key}` when a CSV parses cleanly to zero usable rows.
dependencies: W05-F004 (the row-count floor is the only other net; it also has holes).

title: 9 of 21 registered sources have no row-count floor — deleting ktcSfTep (the retail anchor, 501 rows) from the whole board leaves contractHealth 'healthy' with zero errors
claimUnderTest: 'A source at zero is a hard error (source_missing); below floor is a warning' — the per-source row-count floor is the safety net for a silently dropped source.
observed: `_DEFAULT_SOURCE_ROW_FLOORS` (merged with config/weights/source_row_floors.json) has 13 keys, one of which (`ktc`) is not even a blend source. Nine registry sources have no floor at all: ktcSfTep, fantasyProsSf, fantasyCalc, otcffbSf, fantasyNavigatorSf, pfkDynasty, dlfRookieSf, dlfRookieIdp, flockFantasySfRookies. Stripping each in turn from the live contract and re-running the validator: floored sources (dlfSf, yahooBoone) correctly go status=invalid with source_missing; all six unfloored ones tested stay status=healthy, ok=true, errors=[].

reproduction.command:
.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import sys,json,copy
sys.path.insert(0,'.')
from src.api.data_contract import validate_api_data_contract
base=json.load(open('/tmp/w05_full.json'))
for key in ['ktcSfTep','otcffbSf','fantasyCalc','pfkDynasty','fantasyNavigatorSf','fantasyProsSf','dlfSf','yahooBoone']:
    p=copy.deepcopy(base)
    for r in p['playersArray']:
        for f in ('canonicalSiteValues','sourceRanks','sourceRankMeta','sourceNativeValues','sourceOriginalRanks','effectiveSourceRanks','rawSourceValues'):
            m=r.get(f)
            if isinstance(m,dict): m.pop(key,None)
    p['sourceParseErrors']=[]
    h=validate_api_data_contract(p); print(key, h['status'], h['errors'])
EOF
reproduction.expected: source_missing:{key} for every registered source removed
reproduction.actual: ktcSfTep -> healthy []; otcffbSf -> healthy []; fantasyCalc -> healthy []; pfkDynasty -> healthy []; fantasyNavigatorSf -> healthy []; fantasyProsSf -> healthy []; dlfSf -> invalid ['source_missing:dlfSf']; yahooBoone -> invalid ['source_missing:yahooBoone']

numericProof.formula: floors = _DEFAULT_SOURCE_ROW_FLOORS | config.floors; source_missing fires iff key in floors and count == 0

userImpact: The blend can lose its single retail anchor — the source that sets the top of the 0-9999 scale for every offensive player and one of only two value-direct voters — and every health surface, including the contract's own self-report, says the board is healthy. Users read repriced values with no warning.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding enumerates the floor coverage gap. PRIOR-A25-F14 is about which sources can be flagged from settings.sourceRunSummary, a different mechanism.

whatWorks: The floor mechanism itself is correct and load-bearing where it exists — dlfSf and yahooBoone both produce a hard error and flip the contract to invalid. The config file allows tuning without code change.
rootCause: Floors were added per-incident and the newer sources (FN, PFK, FantasyCalc, OTCFFB, the rookie boards) were deliberately deferred pending a live baseline (comment at data_contract.py:701-708) — a deferral that has outlived the baseline being unavailable.
requiredRepair: Add floors for the nine unfloored keys at ~80% of the counts now measured on the live board (ktcSfTep 400, fantasyProsSf 380, fantasyCalc 315, otcffbSf 275, fantasyNavigatorSf 360, pfkDynasty 380, dlfRookieSf 44, dlfRookieIdp 23, flockFantasySfRookies 60), and add a registry-completeness test that fails when a registered source has no floor.

title: The KTC trade/waiver crowd DB is skipped on EVERY successful KTC scrape — `content` is only bound inside the Strategy-3 fallback, so KTC_ID_TO_NAME is never built and the FAAB crowd factor is unreachable
claimUnderTest: The `partial_run_tolerable:KTC_TradeDB` / `:KTC_WaiverDB` warnings are a tolerable transient on a secondary endpoint, and the KTC crowd-sourced FAAB calibration factor is live.
observed: `scrape_ktc` has three extraction strategies. `content = await page.content()` is assigned ONLY inside Strategy 3, which is guarded by `if not name_map:` (line 2268). The ID-map builder at line 2477 is guarded by `if "content" in dir() and content:` — a check on whether that local was ever bound. So on every run where KTC actually works (Strategy 1 API intercept or Strategy 2 DOM, which is what produced today's 500 rows), `content` is unbound, KTC_ID_TO_NAME stays empty, line 4006's `if SITES.get("KTC") and KTC_ID_TO_NAME` is False, and both crowd endpoints are skipped with the 'no playerID->name mapping available' warning. The condition is inverted: the crowd DB can only run on the degraded path. Downstream, `ktcCrowd` is absent from the live payload, so `crowd_bid_map_from_contract` returns {} and the 'KTC crowd-sourced calibration' factor never appears — and the FAAB response does not list it as missing either (only 4 factors, warnings=[]).

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['source_health']['source_failures'])"; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json'));print('ktcCrowd' in d)"; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Bhayshul Tuten","budgetRemaining":100}' | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([f['label'] for f in d['factors']], d['warnings'])"
reproduction.expected: either a KTC crowd factor in the FAAB breakdown, or an explicit missing:true entry for it
reproduction.actual: source_failures reports both KTC_TradeDB and KTC_WaiverDB 'partial' with valueCount 0 and skipReason missing_ktc_id_map; ktcCrowd not in payload -> False; FAAB factors = ['Player value baseline','Trending bump','League historical calibration','Rival contention'], warnings = []

numericProof.formula: KTC_ID_TO_NAME populated iff Strategy 3 ran iff name_map was empty after Strategies 1+2

userImpact: A user on /waivers gets a FAAB bid whose crowd-calibration input is permanently absent, presented as a complete factor breakdown with no 'missing' marker — the 15%-weight rival-contention factor IS marked missing, so the omission of the crowd factor reads as 'not applicable' rather than 'never collected'. The operator meanwhile sees two permanent amber warnings that are documented as 'tolerable transients'.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the ingestion area covers KTC_TradeDB/KTC_WaiverDB or the crowd-FAAB path.

whatWorks: The whole downstream chain is correctly built and would work the moment the map exists: build_crowd_bid_map, crowd_bid_map_from_contract, the 70/30 blend, the _ktc_crowd_applies guard and the factor emission are all present and unit-tested. The failure is confined to one variable-scope bug in the scraper.
rootCause: `content` is a Strategy-3 local; the ID-map builder guards on its existence with `"content" in dir()` rather than fetching the page source unconditionally. The guard was presumably written when Strategy 3 was the only path.
requiredRepair: Hoist `content = await page.content()` out of the `if not name_map:` block (or build KTC_ID_TO_NAME from the intercepted API payload, which carries playerID+playerName directly), and stop classifying an always-skipped source as a tolerable partial. Separately, have faab_recommender emit the crowd factor with missing:true when the map is empty, matching how rival contention is handled.

title: Only 2 of 21 sources cast any vote on any draft pick, and all 72 slot picks are single-source: a fresh KTC pick value sits unread in canonicalSiteValues while the anchor is IDPTradeCalc alone
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Pick rows widen the anchor set to include ktcSfTep so the two real pick markets (KTC + IDPTC) average as peers.' And the dlfRookieSf registry entry: 'The pick nudge is wired via synthetic "2026 Pick R.SS" rows that the conversion step appends to the CSV so the source's Hill value flows into pick rankDerivedValue directly.'
observed: Counting non-null sourceRanks over the 144 pick rows on the live board: ktcSfTep votes on 36 (the generic Early/Mid/Late 1st-4th tiers, the only picks in ktcSfTep.csv), idpTradeCalc on 96. No other source votes on any pick. All 72 slot picks (2026 Pick 1.01 .. 6.12) have sourceCount == 1 and anchorValue == the IDPTradeCalc value, even though canonicalSiteValues carries a KTC value for every one of them (pickAnchors['ktc'] has 126 entries, interpolated by the scraper) — `ktc` was demoted to a non-voting display key in 2026-04-28 and nothing re-routed the pick anchors to ktcSfTep. Separately, all 55 dlfRookieSf synthetic pick stamps land in canonicalSiteValues (as raw synthetic rank encodings like 999880) but appear in sourceRanks on zero pick rows.

reproduction.command:
curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data' -o /tmp/full.json; python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,collections
pa=json.load(open('/tmp/full.json'))['playersArray']
picks=[r for r in pa if r.get('assetClass')=='pick']
v=collections.Counter()
for r in picks:
  for k,x in (r.get('sourceRanks') or {}).items():
    if x is not None: v[k]+=1
print(len(picks), dict(v))
slot=[r for r in picks if ' Pick ' in r['displayName']]
print(len(slot), collections.Counter(r['sourceCount'] for r in slot))
r=[x for x in slot if x['displayName']=='2026 Pick 1.01'][0]
print(r['canonicalSiteValues'], r['sourceRanks'], r['anchorValue'], r['rankDerivedValue'])
EOF
reproduction.expected: pick rows anchored on the mean of the two real pick markets
reproduction.actual: 144 picks; sourceRanks votes = {'ktcSfTep':36,'idpTradeCalc':96}; 72 slot picks all sourceCount=1; 2026 Pick 1.01 canonicalSiteValues={'ktc':6726,'idpTradeCalc':8013,'dlfRookieSf':999880}, sourceRanks={'idpTradeCalc':12}, anchorValue=8013

numericProof.formula: anchor_value = mean(contributions of is_cross_market sources); with both pick markets voting this would be (6726+8013)/2

userImpact: Every draft pick on /rankings, in the trade calculator and in the draft-capital board is priced by one market, and is flagged sourceCount=1 / isSingleSource=true — which the UI presents as 'speculative'. A user trading a 1.01 sees 7799 where a two-market peer average of the numbers the system already holds would be materially lower (KTC prices it 16% below IDPTC). The docs assert the opposite of what runs.

priorFinding.note: F02 concerns the pick-YEAR discount double-counting, a different stage. Nothing prior covers pick source coverage or the ktc/ktcSfTep pick-anchor split.

whatWorks: The 36 generic tier picks (2026/2027/2028 Early|Mid|Late 1st-4th) genuinely do get both markets: ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc both vote, e.g. 2026 Early 1st = 5605 / 5554. The mechanism is correct where the ktcSfTep CSV happens to carry the row.
rootCause: KTC's slot-pick values reach the contract only through `pickAnchors['ktc']`, which is stamped under the demoted non-voting `ktc` key. ktcSfTep.csv contains only the 36 generic tiers KTC publishes, so the promoted key has nothing to vote with on slot picks. The 2026-04-28 demotion of `ktc` moved the blend vote but not the pick anchors.
requiredRepair: Stamp pickAnchors under `ktcSfTep` as well as `ktc` (KTC's pick board carries no TE dimension, so the two are identical for picks — they already are on all 36 shared rows), or make the pick anchor set read `ktc` explicitly. Then either wire the dlfRookieSf synthetic pick stamps into sourceRanks or stop writing them into canonicalSiteValues and correct the registry comment.
dependencies: Coordinate with the value-pipeline workstream: pick tethering (Phase 5.2b) overwrites current-year slot picks, so measure the effect on 2027/2028 slots separately.

title: The raw-ingest scaffold (/api/scaffold/raw, /status, /identity) serves a 2026-04-20 artifact stamped with a 2026-08-03 mtime, and no code in the tree can produce a new one
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md lists /api/scaffold/raw as 'Raw source snapshots' and /api/scaffold/status as 'Pipeline status' — live operator surfaces.
observed: All three serve run_id 20260420T194828Z, created_at 2026-04-20 — 106 days before the audit date. `/api/scaffold/status` reports `mtime: 2026-08-03T22:00:56` (the git-checkout time of the tracked file), so the one field an operator would read as an age reads as 'yesterday'. No staleness field, no warning: `warnings` is []. The snapshot covers 9 sources, two of which (FANTASYPROS_SF, FLOCK_FANTASY_SF) recorded record_count 0 at capture time with warnings still []. It also carries FOOTBALLGUYS_SF (563) + FOOTBALLGUYS_IDP (525) — 1,088 records from a vendor that is not in _RANKING_SOURCES at all and whose freshness stamp is frozen at 2026-05-24. Grepping the tree for a writer of data/raw_sources/raw_source_snapshot_*.json finds only consumers (server.py, scripts/validate_ingest.py, scripts/identity_resolve.py) and a retention pruner; no producer exists, and no workflow references the scaffold.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/status; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/raw | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['run_id'],d['created_at'],d['warnings']);print([(s['source'],s['record_count']) for s in d['snapshots']])"; grep -rn 'raw_source_snapshot' --include='*.py' . | grep -v tests
reproduction.expected: a snapshot from the last refresh cycle, or an explicit staleness marker
reproduction.actual: run_id 20260420T194828Z, created_at 2026-04-20T19:48:28Z, warnings []; scaffold/status mtime 2026-08-03T22:00:56 with no age field; 9 snapshots incl. FANTASYPROS_SF 0 and FLOCK_FANTASY_SF 0; no producer in the tree

userImpact: Operator-facing only, but actively misleading: the endpoint's own mtime field says the ingest pipeline ran yesterday when it last ran in April, and it names FootballGuys as a contributing source that has not fetched since May and is not in the blend registry at all. `scripts/validate_ingest.py` validates this April artifact and will pass.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced the 106-day staleness and the absent staleness marker. Extending it: there is no producer for data/raw_sources/ anywhere in the tree, so the surface is not merely stale but unrefreshable; and two of the nine snapshotted sources recorded 0 records with warnings still empty. Also confirms PRIOR-A25-F11 (FootballGuys dead, stamp 1779666437 = 2026-05-24T23:47:17Z) from the scaffold side.

whatWorks: Nothing in the frontend consumes /api/scaffold/*, so no user-facing page is showing April data.
rootCause: The scaffold's producer was removed (or never migrated out of the one-off CI run that wrote these files with /home/runner/work/... paths baked in); the read side was left registered.
requiredRepair: Decide: either restore a producer wired into scheduled-refresh.yml, or remove the three routes and validate_ingest.py/identity_resolve.py's dependence on them. In either case have the endpoints report `ageHours` from the snapshot's own `created_at`, not the file mtime, and surface a warning past a threshold.

title: The per-source deploy gate documents itself as running every 6h in health-check.yml; it does not — the 6h workflow uses a floor of 8 covered sources out of 21
claimUnderTest: verify_live_source_coverage.py: 'Used at two layers so a degraded board cannot persist silently: deploy/verify-deploy.sh ... and .github/workflows/health-check.yml — every 6h against the public URL, catching drift that happens outside a deploy.'
observed: `grep -rn verify_live_source_coverage .github/workflows/ deploy/` returns exactly one hit: deploy/verify-deploy.sh:340. health-check.yml instead inlines a dependency-free check with MIN_SOURCES = 8 and MIN_PER_SOURCE = 5 ('Dependency-free so this lean workflow needs no checkout'), which is designed only to separate the healthy ~16-21-source board from the catastrophic 3-source legacy export. Losing any 1 to 13 individual sources between deploys passes that gate. The strict script itself works: run against the live server it prints 'ok: live board carries 21 registered source(s); 0 fresh-but-absent'.

reproduction.expected: the strict fresh-but-absent gate running every 6h against prod
reproduction.actual: one reference only (deploy/verify-deploy.sh:340); health-check.yml uses MIN_SOURCES=8; strict script run manually returns 'ok: live board carries 21 registered source(s); 0 fresh-but-absent (0 skipped: stale/empty)'

numericProof.formula: alert iff count(sources with >=5 covered players) < 8

userImpact: Between deploys (which can be days apart) the board can lose up to 13 of 21 sources without any production alert. The 2h CI watchdog (watchdog_contract_coverage.py) does cover this against the CI checkout, so the exposure is specifically 'the running prod process serves a different board than CI builds'.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the docstring-vs-wiring mismatch for verify_live_source_coverage.py.

whatWorks: Both CI watchdogs pass against the live tree right now: `watchdog_freshness.py` -> 'ok: 22 sources fresh, 0 hard-stale'; `watchdog_contract_coverage.py` -> 'ok: 21 registered source(s) covered, 0 fresh-but-absent'. The deploy-time gate is genuinely wired and would fail a deploy that served a degraded board.
rootCause: The health-check workflow was deliberately kept checkout-free, so the strict script could not be invoked there; the script's docstring was written for the intended design and never corrected.
requiredRepair: Either add a checkout step (or ship the per-source expectations as data in the /api/status payload so a dependency-free checker can be strict), or correct the docstring and lower MIN_SOURCES tolerance to name the expected registry count.

title: Per-source staleness is computed in every /api/data payload and shown to nobody: two disagreeing threshold tables (6h in code, 24h in config) and no user-visible surface for either
claimUnderTest: config/source_staleness.json's own comment: a stale source is 'reported everywhere (on-site stale banner, email alerts ..., the freshness-watchdog summary)'.
observed: There is no on-site per-source stale banner. `dataFreshness.sourceTimestamps` — 22 entries each carrying ageHours, maxAgeHours and staleness fresh|stale|missing — is shipped in every /api/data response and is read by exactly one module in the tree, `src/consensus_edge/service.py`, whose feature flag is OFF by default (ADR-023). The frontend touches `dataFreshness` in one place, rankings/page.jsx:835, and reads only `generatedAt` for a whole-board 'updated Xm ago'. StaleDataBanner polls /api/health and shows a single whole-board `data_age_hours`. Two independent threshold tables disagree by 4x: `_SOURCE_MAX_AGE_HOURS` in data_contract.py sets 6h for ktc/ktcSfTep/idpTradeCalc/dynastyNerdsSfTep/fantasyProsIdp/dynastyDaddySf/fantasyCalc/otcffbSf/draftSharks/draftSharksIdp/fantasyNavigatorSf/pfkDynasty; config/source_staleness.json sets 24h for every source. The 6h table is the one that stamps the payload; the 24h table is the one that fires email. Neither reaches a user. Finally, staleness is purely descriptive: nothing downweights or drops a stale source's vote.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data?view=app' | python3 -c "import json,sys;t=json.load(sys.stdin)['dataFreshness']['sourceTimestamps'];print(len(t));print({k:(v['maxAgeHours'],v['staleness']) for k,v in list(t.items())[:6]})"; grep -rn 'sourceTimestamps' --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' frontend/ | grep -v node_modules; grep -rn 'sourceTimestamps' --include='*.py' src/ | grep -v test
reproduction.expected: a surface where a user or operator sees which individual source is stale
reproduction.actual: 22 sourceTimestamps entries shipped; zero frontend references; one Python consumer (src/consensus_edge/service.py, flag off). maxAgeHours for ktc = 6 while config/source_staleness.json thresholds.ktc = 24.

userImpact: A single dead source (the documented idpShow-cookie-lapse mode) is invisible on-site: the whole-board age stays fresh because 20 other sources refresh, /tools/source-health does not list the source at all (W05-F001), and only an email alert fires — and only if ALERT_TO is configured. Meanwhile that source's last-known values keep voting at full weight.

priorFinding.note: F13 ('staleness is reporting-only; a stale source votes at full weight') reproduced: nothing in _compute_unified_rankings reads sourceTimestamps.staleness. Also PRIOR-A25-F04 ('the contract calls 12 sources stale while the watchdog calls all 22 fresh') is NOT reproducible at HEAD — every source reads fresh under both tables today (all ageHours 1.66-1.86 vs thresholds of 6 and 24), because _build_source_timestamps now prefers the data/scrape_state stamp over CSV mtime. The underlying two-table conflict F04 identified is real and still latent; the divergence it measured is not currently observable.

whatWorks: The email alert path is real and correctly per-source: _build_source_health_snapshot's `sources` block (22 correct entries) feeds src/api/source_health_alerts.check_and_alert from the daily /api/signal-alerts/run sweep, with a documented soft/soft-escalate policy for idpShow. The CI freshness watchdog also runs on the 2h refresh and passes.
rootCause: Per-source freshness grew two independent implementations for two independent consumers (contract payload for consensus_edge; config file for email) and never got a UI.
requiredRepair: Collapse to one threshold source of truth (config/source_staleness.json, via resolve_threshold) and have _build_source_timestamps call it. Then render sourceTimestamps on /tools/source-health as part of the W05-F001 fix.

title: Verified clean: all 21 registered ranking sources have a live fetcher, a fresh CSV, and real votes on the served board — end to end
claimUnderTest: Every source in _RANKING_SOURCES is fetched, stored, read by the blend, and votes on the live board.
observed: Traced all 21 keys through the full chain. Fetcher: 19 have a dedicated scripts/fetch_*.py; ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc are produced by Dynasty Scraper.py. File: every _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS entry resolves to an existing CSV in CSVs/site_raw/ (22 files, all present). Freshness: all 22 report staleness='fresh' with ageHours 1.66-1.86. Blend: every key appears in sourceRanks on the live board with non-null ranks (min 29 rows for dlfRookieIdp, max 903 for idpTradeCalc), and served_source_coverage confirms 21 keys with sourceRankMeta membership. No registered source is dead, and no fetched CSV in CSVs/site_raw/ is unread (the two draftSharksRos* files are consumed by src/ros/sources/draftsharks_ros.py, and ktc.csv is the deliberately non-voting display/arbitrage source).

reproduction.actual: 'ok: live board carries 21 registered source(s); 0 fresh-but-absent (0 skipped: stale/empty)'; 'ok: 22 sources fresh, 0 hard-stale'; 'ok: 21 registered source(s) covered, 0 fresh-but-absent (0 skipped: stale/empty)'

numericProof.formula: chain_complete = fetcher AND csv_exists AND fresh AND sourceRanks_count > 0

userImpact: None — this is the healthy case. Recorded so the negative findings above are read as gaps in REPORTING and in PICK coverage, not as a broken ingestion pipeline.
whatWorks: See observed. Notable per-source detail: KTC's 464 non-pick CSV rows match the player universe at 100%; IDPTradeCalc's 900 rows match 814 (90.4%); the largest apparent losses (fantasyNavigatorSf 758 CSV rows -> 455 board values) are almost entirely retired/off-board players (only 16 of the 303 unmatched sit inside the source's own top 300), i.e. honest coverage, not a matching failure.

title: The reported KTC 590/1074 and IDPTradeCalc 898/1074 coverage is fully explained and correct — the gaps are board depth and the pick-anchor interpolation, not lost data
claimUnderTest: The health check's 'ktc 590 of 1074, idpTradeCalc 898 of 1074' figures indicate missing coverage that needs explaining.
observed: Exact arithmetic identity on the raw 1,074-row universe: ktc 590 = 464 player rows (KTC's 500-row board minus its 36 generic pick tiers; all 464 matched by name) + 126 rows from pickAnchors['ktc'] (the scraper's interpolation of KTC's 36 tiers into slot picks). idpTradeCalc 898 = 814 matched player rows (of 900 scraped) + 84 rows from pickAnchors['idpTradeCalc']. The 483 contract rows with no ktc value break down as 398 IDP (KTC publishes no defenders), 19 K, 50 deep offense past KTC's top-500 cut, 16 unclassified. The 181 with no idpTradeCalc are 48 picks (the 5th/6th-round tiers IDPTC does not price), 76 deep offense, 28 deep IDP, 19 K, 10 unclassified. No source rows are silently lost.

reproduction.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,collections
d=json.load(open('data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json'))
pl=d['players']; pa=d['pickAnchors']
full=json.load(open('/tmp/w05_full.json'))
cls={(r.get('canonicalName') or r.get('displayName')):('pick' if r.get('assetClass')=='pick' else 'player') for r in full['playersArray']}
for k in ('ktc','idpTradeCalc'):
  names=[n for n,p in pl.items() if p.get(k) is not None]
  print(k, len(names), collections.Counter(cls.get(n) for n in names), 'pickAnchors', len(pa[k]))
EOF
reproduction.actual: ktc 590 Counter({'player': 464, 'pick': 126}) pickAnchors 126; idpTradeCalc 898 Counter({'player': 814, 'pick': 84}) pickAnchors 84

userImpact: None — recorded to close the question. The real pick problem is W05-F006 (those 126 KTC pick values do not vote), not a coverage shortfall.

priorFinding.note: Explanatory result requested by the workstream brief.

whatWorks: KTC name matching is 464/464 on non-pick rows. IDPTradeCalc is 814/900; the 86 unmatched are below the board's own inclusion bar.

title: The GitHub-Actions 2h refresh cron misses roughly a quarter of its cycles while the prod systemd fetch timers hit every one
claimUnderTest: 'Runs the scraper + canonical rebuild every 2 hours' (cron '42 */2 * * *').
observed: Reading the commit stream the workflow itself produces ('chore: freshness stamps <UTC>'), over the 26.7h window 2026-08-03T15:37Z to 2026-08-04T18:21Z there are 10 runs where 13-14 are scheduled. Inter-run gaps: 2.87, 1.85, 1.53, 2.08, 4.00, 3.50, 3.75, 4.00, 3.13 hours — three gaps at or above 3.5h and one full missed cycle. Over the same window the prod-side systemd fetch timers land exactly on cadence (dlf at :27 and idpShow at :32 of every even UTC hour, 14/14 runs, zero misses).

reproduction.command: git log --since='2026-08-02' --format='%s' -- data/scrape_state | grep 'freshness stamps' | head -20

userImpact: Board data is up to 4h old rather than 2h at the worst points. Not a correctness defect, but it interacts with W05-F009: the 6h maxAgeHours budgets in _SOURCE_MAX_AGE_HOURS assume a 2h cadence ('6 hours ≈ three missed cycles'); at the observed cadence a 6h budget is closer to 1.5 missed cycles of headroom.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced with a different window and method (workflow-authored commit timestamps rather than run history). My measurement is 10/13 (~23% missed) over 26.7h. Confidence is medium rather than high because the commit stream is a proxy for the run stream — a run that produced no stamp change would not appear — though the workflow force-adds data/scrape_state/ every run, so that should be rare.

whatWorks: The prod-side systemd fetch timers (dlf, idpShow) are perfectly regular over the same window, so this is specific to GitHub Actions' documented best-effort cron.
rootCause: GitHub Actions schedule events are best-effort and are dropped under load; nothing compensates.
requiredRepair: Either accept and document the real cadence (and widen the freshness budgets that assume 2h), or move the scrape trigger to the prod host's systemd timers, which are demonstrably reliable here, with Actions as a backstop.
